html:
Khwarazm, or Chorasmia, is a large oasis on the delta of the Amu Darya, south of the Aral Sea, in what is now Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. The map shows it around 700, when it was a kingdom ruled by the Afrighid shahs from their capital at Kath.

Its people spoke Khwarezmian, an Iranian language, and lived from irrigated farming and trade between the steppe and Iran. In 712 the Arab general Qutayba ibn Muslim conquered it during the Arab conquests. Later the scholar al-Biruni, a native of Khwarazm, wrote that the conquerors had killed its learned men and burned its books.

Under Islam it kept its own rulers and became a centre of science. The mathematician al-Khwarizmi, whose name gave us the word algorithm, took his name from it. In 995 the rulers of Gurganj replaced the old shahs. Two centuries later Khwarazm was the core of the Khwarazmian Empire, destroyed when the Mongols invaded in 1219 to 1221. See also the later Khanate of Khiva.
